beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Name this flat patch by counting its straight sides.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A polygon is flat, closed, and has straight sides that never cross.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Closed means no gap. A side is one straight part of the outline.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A corner is where two sides meet. Each side reaches one new corner.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: From the ring: one side, one corner.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two sides, two corners.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three sides, three corners.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four sides, four corners.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Five sides, five corners.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back at the start. Stop here: five sides in all.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The opening inside a corner is an angle. Five corners, five angles.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A polygon with five sides is a pentagon.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Turning it or having unequal sides does not change its name.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Move this corner inward.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: That corner went inside. I think it is gone.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two sides meet here, so this is a corner too.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Follow the outline into and out of the dent.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One, two, three, four, five in all.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Five corners in all. It is a pentagon.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One, two, three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three sides: a triangle.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One, two, three, four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four sides: a quadrilateral.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One, two, three, four, five, six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six sides: a hexagon.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Eight sides: an octagon.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which shape has exactly seven angles?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight angles.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: B: one, two, three, four, five angles.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: C: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven angles.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: D: one, two, three angles.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: I counted seven around C, so I choose C.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Every side leads to a corner.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One angle at each corner. Five sides: this is a pentagon.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count once around. Each side leads to a corner, even at a dent.
